items.q: Should I form a team with the same card type (Happy, Cute, Pure)?
items.a: No. Count how many of each type your leader skill and passives need, and fill those counts.
items.why: Type does nothing by itself; songs carry no type in the game data. It matters only through skills: 26 leader skills need a minimum number of one type, and most stat and Score Support passives hit "2 members of type X". A 2-2-1 or 3-2 split often switches on more passives than a mono-type team.
items.when: If your leader needs 3 or more of one type, meet that first and fit passives around it.

items.q: Should I form a team with the same main stat?
items.a: Yes, when your leader buffs one stat. Match everyone’s main stat to it. With an all-stats or Score Support leader, it matters much less.
items.why: Overall Power adds Performance, Technique and Sense equally, so no stat is better on its own. But single-stat leader skills are the biggest buff in the game: +80% to +135% of one stat for the whole unit on 5★ cards. A card’s main stat is about 41–46% of its stats and its weakest about 25–29%, so a mismatched member gets far less.
items.when: All-stats leaders (+30% to +50%) treat every stat equally. Score Support leaders (+60%) don’t touch stats.

items.q: When should I use a card with a different main stat?
items.a: When it brings something a matched card can’t: a needed type or group count, a skill that fills a coverage gap, or a self all-stats or Score Support passive.
items.why: A mismatch only shrinks the leader’s stat buff. Under a +130% leader it costs about 1.5–2.6% of Unit Score, and less as your boards fill (see the Bloom question). A passive that switches on (+2 to +4.5%) or a skill that closes a coverage gap is often worth more.
items.when: Under an all-stats or Score Support leader the cost is close to zero, so pick on skills alone.

items.q: Should I prioritise Bloom 1 and 2 cards over unbloomed ones, even with a different main stat or an inactive passive?
items.a: Usually yes, unless the leader buffs one of the Bloom 1 card’s weakest stats, the buff is around +130%, and your boards are still light. Keep passives working first.
items.why:
Unit Score = Overall Power × 2.037 × (1 + Score Bonus), so every change is a % of Unit Score.

Change on one cardUnit Score
Bloom 1 (active skill level 2)+2.0%
Bloom 2 (+10% stats)+1.7 to +1.9%
Leader buffs the card’s second stat−1.1 to −2.1%
Leader buffs the card’s weakest stat−1.3 to −2.6%
Stat passive doesn’t activate−3 to −4%
items.how:
• Bloom 1 only raises the active skill’s Score Up (usually +20 points). The Unit Score formula on 1,200 random 5★ units gave a median of +2.0%. It counts twice, because the Special line scales with the Active line.
  • A mismatch only shrinks the leader’s stat buff. Board stats, Memory Bonus and passives grow Overall Power without it, so it matters less as boards fill:
Leader buff, weakest statNo boardsBlue doneRed + Blue full
+80%−1.8%−1.6%−1.4%
+100%−2.1%−1.9%−1.6%
+130%−2.6%−2.3%−2.0%

Only the +130% row, before Red is built, costs more than Bloom 1’s +2.0%.
items.when: In a real song only the strongest active skill counts, so Bloom 1 on a card usually overlapped by a stronger skill gains less than Unit Score suggests.

items.q: Which passive is best for Unit Score: stat up on 2 members, Score Support on 2 members, or all stats on one?
items.a: Stat up on 2 members’ main stat, then all stats on self, then stat up on an off stat, then Score Support. The order holds at every board stage.
items.why:
Passive (5★, level 2, +130% leader)No boardsFull boards
Stat up, 2 members, main stat+4.5%+3.4%
All stats, self+4.0%+3.0%
Stat up, 2 members, off stat+2.8%+2.1%
Score Support, 2 members+1.6%+1.5%
items.how:
• Stat passives come from the cards’ own stats, so boards dilute them like the leader buff.
  • Score Support is diluted too: Red boards add +20–30% Score Support for the whole unit, and all Score Support adds together. It also misses the Special line, which follows only the base Active line. Medians of 500 random 5★ units.

Boards narrow the gap from about 3× to 2×, but Score Support never overtakes a working stat passive.
items.when: Use Score Support as a tiebreaker: about +1.7% on your two strongest skills, about +1.2% with a Score Support leader.

items.q: If more members qualify for a passive than it can buff, which members get it?
items.a: The strongest qualifying members, by what the passive boosts. On a tie, the member earlier in the unit gets it.
items.why:
• Single-stat passive (for example Technique up on 2 members): the qualifying members with the highest value of that stat.
  • All-stats passive: the qualifying members with the highest total stats.
  • Score Support passive: the qualifying members with the highest active skill bonus (Score Up).

In every case a tie goes to whichever card is earlier in the unit.
items.when: This is another reason main stats matter: a card whose main stat isn’t the boosted stat often loses the passive to a teammate who does have it as their main stat. Unit order only decides ties.

items.q: What do the stats actually do?
items.a: Treat Performance + Technique + Sense as one total. Only push one stat when your leader or passives buff it.
items.why: Overall Power adds the three stats with equal weight, and every note’s score scales directly with Overall Power. No stat has a separate effect on score in the game data.

items.q: What is Unit Score, and why is higher better?
items.a: Unit Score = Overall Power × 2.037 × (1 + Score Bonus). Use it to compare units quickly, then check your target song.
items.why: It matches the in-game Unit Score Details screen. Both parts also drive real song score, so a higher Unit Score usually means a higher song score.
items.when: Unit Score assumes a fixed 200-second song with skills firing at their average rate. Your real song may favour a different unit.

items.q: What are Overall Power and Score Bonus, and how do they affect my song score?
items.a: Overall Power is the unit’s strength; Score Bonus is the extra score from skills. Every note scales with Overall Power, and Score Bonus multiplies on top.
items.why:
Overall Power adds

  • Member Parameter (stats from level and Bloom)
  • Outfit Skill (leader stat buff)
  • Passive Skill (stat passives)
  • Holomem Board Bonus (Red, Blue, Green)
  • Memory Bonus and Member Power-Up Bonus

Score Bonus adds

Active, Outfit (leader Score Support), Passive (Score Support), Board and Special lines.

Per note: Overall Power × difficulty multiplier × (1 + combo bonus) × (1 + active skill bonus) × (1 + Yellow bonus).

items.q: How do I increase Overall Power efficiently?
items.a: Fix team choices first, then level, then boards. Matching main stats and keeping passives active cost nothing; levels and a strong leader buff are the biggest levers.
items.why:
LeverOverall Power
Leader buff +80% → +130% (same stat)+11 to +15%
Red board on the leader (stats only)+17%, +23% if she sings
Whole unit Lv70 → Lv80+10.5 to +12%
Blue Stats Only on all five members+8%
A stat passive switched on (2 members, main stat)+3.7 to +4.7%
One card: 4★ max → 5★ Lv80+3.1 to +3.5%
One card: main stat matches the leader (vs weakest stat)+2.0 to +2.6%
One card: +10 levels+2.0 to +2.4%
One card: Bloom 2 (+10% stats)+1.9 to +2.1%
+1% Member Power-Up Bonus+0.9 to +1.0%
Green gen bonus (2 gen-mates in unit)+0.7 to +0.9%
+1% Memory Bonus+0.4 to +0.6%

Ranges run from a fresh account (no boards, memory or power-up) to a built one (full Red and Blue, memory 5.6%, power-up 10%).
items.how:
• The leader buff multiplies the stat it targets on all five members, which is why matching main stats and a big buff matter so much.
  • Each level adds the same stats (about 250 per level on a 5★), but EXP cost climbs steeply: Lv70→80 costs about 4× the EXP of Lv40→50. Raise your lowest cards first.
  • Board stats, Memory Bonus and passives add to Overall Power without boosting the leader buff, so each one dilutes the others a little as your account grows.
items.when: Overall Power isn’t the whole story. Yellow (+7.5–10% song score), Score Support from Red boards and leaders, and Bloom 1 all raise your score without moving Overall Power. See board setups for where board points pay off most.

items.q: Does a higher Score Bonus always mean a higher song score?
items.a: No. When two units are close, run both on your target song in Hoshidori.
items.why:
1. Only the strongest active skill counts at any moment, so overlaps waste uptime.
  2. Skills on during dense note sections earn more.
  3. Special skills fire at the song’s own special skill activation points.
  4. Activation is random, so runs vary.

A unit can also gain Score Bonus by giving up Overall Power. If the power loss is larger, the song score drops.

items.q: Does the position of my members in my unit matter?
items.a: Yes. Put your strongest special skills on the song’s densest special skill activation points (often the 4th and 5th, but check the song), and keep combo-100 specials out of the first position.
items.why: Members’ special skills fire at the song’s five special skill activation points in unit order: first member at the first point, and so on. A special boosts whatever active skill is on for 10–14 seconds, so where it lands decides how many notes it boosts.
items.when: A special is wasted if no active skill is on during its window, so plan coverage around the activation points too. If two active skills tie on bonus, the member earlier in the unit wins. Life-gated specials (life 600 or 1,000+) are the reverse of combo-gated ones: safer early, before you take damage.
items.how:
• Density matters most. Across 44 songs on Expert, the best activation point is worth a median 40% more than the worst (up to about 3×). Point 4 or 5 is strongest in 26 of 44 songs, but every point wins somewhere.
  • Combo conditions: 5 specials need combo 100+ for their +50–55% activation-chance bonus. On Expert, combo is still under 100 at the first point in 18 of 44 songs (34 of 44 on Hard), even with a clean start. By the second point it’s past 100 on every Expert song. The main Score Up boost still works either way.
  • Combo bonus gives the 5th point about 5–6% more than the 1st. A useful tiebreaker, much smaller than density.

items.q: What are special skills, and how do they work with active skills?
items.a: A special skill is a booster for active skills. Plan for an active skill to be on during each special’s window.
items.why: For 10–14 seconds after its special skill activation point, a special raises the Score Up of whatever active skill is on: +115% to +160% on 5★ cards. Some also add +40% to +55% activation chance. With no active skill on, the special is wasted. In Unit Score, the Special line scales with your Active line.

items.q: What is skill coverage, and why is it important?
items.a: Coverage is the share of the song with at least one active skill on. Gaps earn no skill bonus at all.
items.why: Only the strongest active skill counts at a time, so overlaps are wasted too. A 5★ active skill is on only 32–47% of the time, so several skills must take turns. On KANADE, the best 4-member core covered 96.7% with no frequency nodes and 99.2% with 4.

items.q: What should I look out for to get good skill coverage?
items.a: Mix cooldowns, cover the opening, and check where the gaps fall, not just the percentage.
items.why:
• Two skills with the same cooldown overlap every time.
  • Each skill first fires one cooldown in, so bring a 15–18 second cooldown for the opening.
  • A gap in a dense section or special skill window costs more than one in a quiet part.
  • Use frequency nodes to shift timing, one at a time.
  • Skills fire about 46–55% of the time, so coverage is a best-case plan.

items.q: Should I sacrifice coverage for an active skill with a better score bonus?
items.a: For small gaps, yes. 15 more points of Score Up (e.g. 100% vs 85%) is worth about 8 seconds of gap on a 150-second song.
items.why: A skill with 37% uptime and +15 points raises your song-wide average by about 5.5 points. Each uncovered second costs about 0.7 points of average. That holds only while the stronger skill is the top one on.
items.when: Protect coverage on special skill windows and dense sections, where gaps cost more.

items.q: Are there board setups (leader + member + all member + content) I should aim for?
items.a: Red for leaders, Yellow for singers, Green for gens, Blue for the rest. Board points belong to each holomem, so decide per holomem: a leader fills Red first, then Yellow; a member fills Yellow, then Green’s gen bonus, then Blue.
items.why:
PresetPointsSong scorePer 10 pts
Red Singer – Minimum (leader sings)91+24%+2.7%
Red Singer – Full Bonus (leader sings)141+35%+2.5%
Yellow Solo 10% (her solo songs)35+7.5%+2.1%
Red Non-Singer – Full Bonus126+25%+2.0%
Yellow Unit Only (unit songs)28+4%+1.4%
Green Gen Bonus Only (2 gen-mates in unit)20+0.9 to +1.4%+0.5 to +0.7%
Blue Stats Only (one member)72+2.6%+0.4%
Green Minimum5~0%~0%
items.how:
• Red applies to all five members and adds up to +30% Score Support on top of stats, so it is the biggest lever. Its singer nodes only work when the leader sings the song; otherwise take Non-Singer – Full Bonus.
  • Yellow multiplies every note’s score directly (+7.5% Yellow = +7.5% song score), and works even when the singer isn’t in your unit. It doesn’t show in Overall Power, and Unit Score undersells it.
  • Green’s gen bonus boosts every member of that gen, up to 900 each across your roster, for 20 points.
  • Blue adds the most Overall Power per holomem but only boosts that one card, and does nothing while she is your leader.

Figures: each preset’s nodes from the game data, on a Lv80 unit with a +130% leader, memory 5.6% and power-up 10%; skill effects are medians of 300 random 5★ units.
items.when: Yellow’s Solo 10% preset reaches 7.5% from nodes; the last 2.5% comes from connect effects. If a holomem is the only one from her gen in your unit, Blue beats Green’s gen bonus for her.

items.q: Are there good breakpoints and character levels to aim for?
items.a: Aim for the Holomem Rank and Dream Rank each holomem’s role needs. From Rank 30 board points come fastest (10 per rank). Cards have no special level breakpoints: raise your lowest cards first.
items.why:
Role (Player Guide template)Holomem RankDream RankBoard points

Dream Rank milestones (your account level) unlock parts of every holomem’s board:

  • 10: Red connect slot
  • 15: Blue connect slot
  • 20: Yellow connect slot
  • 25: Red’s 2★ nodes, needed for a full Red board
  • 30: Green’s gen-bonus nodes
items.how: Board points come from Holomem Rank: 2 per rank-up at first, then 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8, and 10 per rank from Rank 30. That totals 26 points at Rank 10, 83 at Rank 20, 161 at Rank 30, 261 at Rank 40 and 361 at Rank 50. A full board costs 453, so no holomem can unlock everything. The totals assume a holomem starts with 0 points at Rank 1 (not yet checked in-game).
items.when: Holomem Rank comes from achievement EXP, and today’s content caps most holomems at Rank 41–45, so Oshi (Rank 43) may not be reachable yet for holomems with few cards or solo songs. The Holomem Rank Calc (Tools menu) shows where each holomem stands. For card upgrades, Bloom 1 and 2 are the efficient early Blooms (see the Bloom question); for where to spend board points, see board setups.

items.q: Why do my Score Bonus and Unit Score drop when I unlock a frequency-up node?
items.a: The node shifts every later activation. Unlock frequency nodes one at a time and lock any that lower Score Bonus.
items.why: Each node shortens that member’s cooldown by about 4%. Windows that filled gaps can slide on top of another member’s skill, leaving new gaps. In Unit Score, overlapping skills with combined activation chance over 100% are averaged, so a weaker skill on top of a stronger one pulls it down.
items.when: On KANADE, the best cores peaked at 4 frequency nodes; more never helped.

items.q: If I want to score high on a certain song, what should I consider?
items.a: Power first, then the song’s type and singers, then skill timing.
items.why:
1. Overall Power: every note scales with it (see how to raise it efficiently). It doesn’t include Yellow or Score Support, so don’t judge boards by it alone (see board setups).
  2. Yellow Score Bonus nodes of the song’s type (solo, group, all) on the singers’ boards, up to 10%. Singers don’t need to be in your unit.
  3. Skills on during the song’s dense sections.
  4. Special skill activation points.
  5. Difficulty multiplier.

items.q: Should I push score on a lower difficulty if I can’t full combo the higher one?
items.a: Usually no: stay on the harder chart. Where you break matters more than how often, and about 100 Greats cost as much as a mid-song break or two. Mark your usual breaks and Greats below to check your song.
items.why:
Higher difficulty multiplies every note’s score, and longer charts build more combo bonus (up to +10% at 1,000 combo). On a full combo the harder chart scores 3–7% more.

A break costs you the combo bonus on every note after it, until your combo climbs back, so its cost depends on when it happens:

Where the break happensCost of one break
Before the 1st special skill activation point0.4–0.7%
1st → 2nd point1.2–1.7%
Middle of the song (2nd → 4th point)1.9–2.5%
4th → 5th point1.5–2.0%
After the 5th point0.6–0.8%

Extra breaks in a stretch where you’ve already broken cost little, because your combo is already low.

Greats score 80% of a Perfect (Perfect and Perfect+ score the same), and only taps and hold starts can be judged Great. Each Great costs about 0.03% of your score (0.02–0.04% depending on the song), so 100 Greats cost about 3%. Harder charts usually bring more Greats, which eats into their lead.
items.when: Greats keep your combo (confirmed); the calculator spreads them evenly through the chart. The calculator doesn’t weight skills: breaking or getting Greats during a special skill window, or breaking while a combo-gated active skill is on, costs more than shown.
items.how:
• Cost of one break at every second, across 46 songs on Expert, using the game’s note weights (hold ticks count 10% of a tap): the worst moment is usually right around the halfway mark; the first and last few seconds cost under 0.1%.
  • On yumeiro wonder, Expert with 4 breaks all in the final stretch still beats a Hard full combo by 3.9%. With 4 breaks all mid-song the lead shrinks to 0.2%.
  • On SPARKS, Expert’s 3.4% lead over a Hard full combo is gone at about 100 Greats; on yumeiro wonder 100 Greats only cut its 5.2% lead to 3.5%, because the song has more notes.

items.q: Why should I run multi lives instead of solo lives when grinding event points?
items.a: Because in a multi live your event points also count the whole room’s score, Fever included. With the same unit and the same score, a multi live earns about 1.6–1.8× the points of a solo live.
items.why:
Event points start from a base value. In solo it depends only on your score. In a multi live the room’s score is added on top (see how event points are calculated). An example with a 2.07M score:

Live typeBasevs solo
Solo258×1.00
Multi, Spotlight (room of 5, 12.1M room score)420×1.63
Multi, Point Rally / Score Challenge (same room)460×1.78

In that run about 61% of the points had nothing to do with the player’s own score: 29% from the fixed 120, 24% from the other four players and 8% from Fever.
items.how:
Fever switches on when the room fills the Fever gauge. Every Perfect fills it fully, a Great 90% and a Good 60%. Auto notes count as Perfects. The room needs 70–90% of a perfect run’s gauge, and the bar rises for longer songs and fuller rooms.

During the Fever stretch (about 15 seconds; in Gate Open: START! it runs from 38.3 s to 53.6 s), every note scores extra. In a full room that came to about +250% per note, which looks like +50% for each player in the room. This size is an estimate from one run and is still being tested.
items.when: A room full of strong units earns you more even if your own unit is weaker, so a room that keeps hitting notes (and triggers Fever) matters as much as your own score.

items.q: Why is choosing Highlight better than selecting the event song itself?
items.a: Highlight gives a fixed song-length bonus that beats every normal song, even the longest ones. It picks a random song sung by the event holomem (unit or solo) and plays it in full.
items.why:
Event points are multiplied by a song-length bonus. A normal song earns about 0.526% per second beyond 90 seconds, scaled by how many Live Boosts you use. Highlight replaces that with a fixed bonus:

SongLength1 boost2–3 boosts4+ boosts
Typical song128 s+26%+24%+20%
Gate Open: START!145 s+38%+35%+29%
Longest songs (KANADE, We are GAMERS !!!!)166 s+52%+48%+40%
Highlightany+54%+50%+42%

Against a typical song, Highlight earns about 22% more points per live with 1 boost. Even the longest songs fall 2 points short.
items.how:
Song-length bonus for a normal song = (seconds − 90) × 0.526% × 1.3 with 1 boost, × 1.2 with 2–3 boosts, × 1.0 with 4 or more, rounded up. Songs of 90 seconds or less get no bonus. The longest songs (166 s) reach exactly +40% at 4+ boosts, which suggests the game sets that cap and puts Highlight just above it.

Checked against two real Highlight runs (1 and 4 boosts), which matched to the exact point.
items.when: Highlight plays the full song, so it costs no extra time. The only reason to pick the event song is if you want a particular chart, for example to push its high-score ranking.

items.q: How are event points calculated for each live?
items.a: Event points = (base × event bonus, rounded up) × song-length bonus × Live Boost × 2 with HoloPassport, rounded up. The base depends on your score and, in multi lives, the room’s score.
items.why:
Live typeBase
Solo120 + your score ÷ 15,000
Multi, Point Rally and Score Challenge120 + your score ÷ 15,000 + room score ÷ 60,000
Multi, Spotlight120 + your score ÷ 15,000 + room score ÷ 75,000

Room score is the Multi Score at the top of the results screen: all five players’ scores plus Fever. Auto Live scores count in full.

Event bonus is 1 + the Earned Bonus shown on the results screen (for example +120% → ×2.2). See how event bonuses work.

Song-length bonus: see Highlight.

Live Boost (the “Rewards ×” number):

Boosts12345678910
Rewards×8×16×24×30×37×42×46×50×53×56

The first three boosts add ×8 each; after that each extra boost adds less, down to ×3 for the tenth.

Event Badges = event points ÷ 10, rounded up.
items.how:
A real Spotlight run (Highlight, 1 boost, HoloPassport): own score 2,086,000, room score 11,951,716, Earned Bonus +120%.

  • Base = 120 + 139.07 + 159.36 = 418.42
  • × 2.2 = 920.53 → 921
  • × 1.54 (Highlight) × 8 (Live Boost) × 2 (HoloPassport) = 22,693.4 → 22,694, exactly what the game showed.

A second run with 4 boosts also matched exactly. The Spotlight formula is confirmed; the Point Rally and Score Challenge divisor (60,000) is still to be checked against a screenshot.

items.q: What types of events are there?
items.a: Three: Point Rally, Score Challenge and Spotlight.
items.why:
• Point Rally (sometimes called Point Race): rank by total Event Pts. Each Event Set Piece also has its own high-score ranking.
  • Score Challenge (sometimes called High Score): rank by your best scores on the Event Set Pieces, with a ranking on the total of those bests.
  • Spotlight (sometimes called Relay): one chapter per holomem, each with its own Event Pts ranking, high-score ranking and badges.
items.when: Point Rally and Spotlight reward volume, so event bonus and multi lives matter most. Score Challenge rewards your best score, so build for score there (see event bonus or Unit Score).

items.q: How do the event card bonuses work?
items.a: Each card in your unit adds its bonuses, and the total is your Earned Bonus. Event points and badges are multiplied by 1 + that total, so +120% means ×2.2.
items.why:
• Member Bonus: the event’s banner cards, usually the cards in that event’s gacha banner. Each one in your unit adds the bonus on the event page (+50% each in Whistling WindWalk).
  • holomem Bonus: each card of the event’s holomem in your unit adds it, whether it’s 3★, 4★ or 5★ (+50% each for Pavolia Reine in Whistling WindWalk). The event holomem’s own banner card counts for both, so it alone gives +100%.
  • Bloom Bonus: every card in your unit adds a bonus for its Bloom level, set by its rarity:
RarityBloom 1Bloom 2Bloom 3Bloom 4Bloom 5
3★+1%+1%+2%+2%+3%
4★+6%+7%+8%+9%+10%
5★+15%+18%+22%+26%+30%
  • Score Bonus: a temporary score boost on the Event Set Pieces when eligible members are in your unit. It raises score, not the Earned Bonus.
  • Minigame Bonus: more rewards from eligible minigames.

Member, holomem and Bloom bonuses raise points and badges, not score, and they all add together. Checked example: a Reine card (not the banner one, Bloom 0) +50%, plus 5★ cards at Bloom 2, 1, 1 and 3 (+18, +15, +15, +22) = +120%, and the points matched ×2.2 exactly.
items.when: Bloom counts for every card, banner or not, so blooming your strongest 5★ cards raises event points in every event. Because bonuses add up, each extra card is worth less in relative terms as the total grows: going from +100% to +130% is ×2.0 → ×2.3, or +15%.

items.q: Is it better to stack event point bonuses or increase Unit Score during event point grinding?
items.a: Stack event bonus in Point Rally and Spotlight. A banner or event-holomem card adds +50% Earned Bonus (+100% if it’s both), usually +15–45% points, while losing 5% of your score costs only about 2% in a multi live. In Score Challenge, build for score.
items.why:
Event bonus multiplies the whole base. Your own score is only part of the base, so a change in score moves points by much less:

Live typeYour score’s share of the base+10% score gives
Soloabout 54%+5.3%
Multi, Spotlightabout 39%+3.9%
Multi, Point Rallyabout 37%+3.7%

(Figures for a 2.07M score in a room of similar players.)

A banner card adds +50% to the Earned Bonus. Going from +100% to +150% is ×2.0 → ×2.5, or +25% points; the event holomem’s banner card (+100%) makes it +50%. To lose 25% of points in a multi live, the swap would have to cost over half your score. Even a Bloom difference matters: swapping a Bloom 0 5★ for a Bloom 5 5★ adds +30%.
items.how:
Rule of thumb: a bonus card is worth it when its bonus ÷ (1 + your current Earned Bonus) is bigger than 0.4 × the % of score it costs (0.55 in solo).

The in-game Prioritize Event Bonus option builds a bonus-first unit for you.
items.when: Score Challenge ranks by score, so event bonus doesn’t help there; keep only the Score Bonus cards for the Event Set Pieces.

items.q: How big is the difference in event points between Auto and manual play in multi lives?
items.a: Small: an all-Perfect full combo earns about 11–12% more points than Auto, and a realistic manual run about 6–9% more.
items.why:
Auto scores every note at 80% of a Perfect and gets no combo bonus. That works out to about 77% of an all-Perfect full combo on Expert (75–78% across 46 songs; 77–79% on Hard). Skills still fire, but Judgement Boost and life recovery do nothing and Perfect-only effects are weaker.

Your score is only about 40% of a multi live’s event points (see event bonus or Unit Score), so a 23% lower score costs far less in points. Example: Auto scored 2.07M; an all-Perfect full combo would be about 2.68M.

Live typeAll-Perfect FC vs Auto
